Ported native git invocations across the tool suite from the PowerShell & call operator to Diagnostics.Process (stderr captured via .NET), since Set-StrictMode/ErrorActionPreference=Stop can promote a harmless git stderr warning (e.g. core.autocrlf CRLF notices) into a terminating error that survives even a local 2>$null redirect in some hosts; also fixed two BOM-less non-ASCII source files that parsed differently under Windows PowerShell 5.1's default (non-UTF8) script-loading encoding, a String.Contains(string, StringComparison) call that is .NET 5+ only, and an over-eager session-reconciliation heuristic that could reap a still-in-use session. Documented workflow/index-pipeline/task-lifecycle behavior and output shapes are unchanged; this is exclusively a portability and process-invocation-safety change.
